headline: Beats 360 Review | Raises the bar for premium lifestyle headphones

Premium headphones have evolved from being primarily about sound to becoming an everyday device that needs to get several things right. Comfort, ANC, call quality, battery life and how well they fit into an active lifestyle now matter just as much. That is also why the premium headphones space has become increasingly competitive, with brands finding different ways to make their products stand out.

The Beats 360 enters this space at ₹42,900, bringing interchangeable earcup and headband cushions, IPX4 resistance and a design aimed at both workouts and everyday use. These additions give the Beats 360 a distinct identity, but the bigger question is how well that approach works in daily use. And with the Sony WH-1000XM6 and Sennheiser HDB 630 also competing in this price range, the Beats 360 has some serious benchmarks to contend with.

So, let’s find out if the Beats 360 has what it takes to stand out.

The biggest change with the Beats 360 is its approach to design. Beats has made the earcups and headband cushions removable, which gives you more flexibility than most premium headphones. You get Performance Knit cushions for workouts and UltraPlush cushions for everyday listening.

I particularly like this idea because it makes sense beyond just customisation. The Performance Knit material is better suited to an active session, while the softer UltraPlush option makes more sense when you are working or travelling. It gives the Beats 360 two personalities without changing the headphones themselves.

The IPX4 rating also adds some much-needed practicality. Sweat and water resistance is still uncommon among premium over-ear headphones. That gives the Beats 360 an advantage if you plan to use them during workouts.
